note: Maryland reports abuse to the local department of social services or to local police rather than to a single statewide intake, though 1-800-91-PREVENT will take the call. It also licenses Residential Child Care programs as their own category through the Department of Human Services. One useful piece of Maryland law: since October 2016, where a local department believes a mandated reporter knowingly failed to report, it must file a complaint with that reporter's own licensing board.

channels.name: Maryland Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines professional counselors and therapists, including marriage and family therapists and alcohol and drug counselors. Where the Board votes to investigate, it assigns its own investigator, and a thorough investigation has to come before any charge against a licensee.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It says many financial and interpersonal issues fall outside its jurisdiction because no breach of the Professional Counselors Act is involved. It cannot help you sue for money or settle a fee dispute.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed counselor or therapist in Maryland. Psychologists and social workers have separate boards.
channels.how: File through the Board's complaint gateway. Complaints are taken from patients, family members and any other member of the public.

channels.name: Maryland Board of Examiners of Psychologists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists and registered psychology associates in Maryland.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist or registered psychology associate.
channels.how: Complete the Board's complaint form - there are separate written instructions for filling it in - and send it to the Board.

channels.name: Maryland DHS, Licensing and Monitoring (Residential Child Care)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and monitors Residential Child Care programs in Maryland as a distinct category, and takes complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed residential child care program.
channels.how: Contact the Department of Human Services.

channels.name: Maryland child abuse and neglect reporting
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a child protective services investigation. Reports go to the local department of social services for the county the child is in, or to local law enforcement.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Maryland program.
channels.how: Call the local department of social services, or 1-800-91-PREVENT, or 911 in an emergency. Report orally straight away; a mandated reporter must also file a written report within 48 hours.

channels.name: Disability Rights Maryland
channels.what_it_can_do: Maryland's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Maryland program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
